claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with my first question:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm asking because I have a child and I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for that information. That's helpful context.

To assess your eligibility, I need to learn more about your child and your circumstances.

**What is your child's name and how old are they?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: My child's name is Alex and they're 15 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's useful information.

**Are you living with Alex, or does Alex live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good to know. 

**Are you currently responsible for Alex's care and upkeep (for example, providing food, clothes, pocket money, and a place to live)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm responsible for Alex's care. I provide everything they need - food, clothes, and they live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's very helpful.

**Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or are you a UK citizen?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a couple more questions to ensure I have the full picture.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, or an apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one final question to complete my assessment.

**Has Alex started any paid work, or is Alex receiving any benefits in their own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't started any paid work and isn't receiving any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect, I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Yes, you are eligible for Child Benefit!**

You meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex:

- ✓ You live in the UK
- ✓ You are responsible for Alex (providing food, clothes, and accommodation)
- ✓ You live with Alex
- ✓ Alex is under 16 years old
- ✓ Alex has no circumstances that would prevent eligibility

You should be able to make a claim for Child Benefit. If you haven't already, you can apply through the official government channels.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
